Theme

Money, work & business

donate verb

also donation, make a donation, give to charity, contribute money

classical

Suet. Aug. 57.2: prō facultāte quisque pecūniās contulērunt, each gave money as he could afford
Liv. 26.36: in pūblicum cōnferāmus, let us give it to the treasury

cōnferō, cōnferre, contulī, collātum

verb, conjugation

give (money to a cause), contribute

The gift in the accusative, the cause after in or ad: pecūniam in rem cōnferre. A small coin given is a stips (see alms).

Other words

  • dōnō, dōnāre, dōnāvī, dōnātum — give as a present

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.5.65–66: dōnāsset jamne catēnam ex vōtō Laribus, whether he had yet given his chain to the household gods, as he had vowed

    To give as a present (see give), to a person or to the gods.

Examples

  • In restitūtiōnem Palātīnae domūs incendiō absūmptae veterānī, decuriae, tribūs atque etiam singillātim ē cēterō genere hominum libentēs ac prō facultāte quisque pecūniās contulērunt

    For the rebuilding of his house on the Palatine, which had burned down, the veterans, the guilds, the tribes and individuals of every other sort gave money, gladly and each as he could affordSuet. Aug. 57.2

See also give, gift, alms, fund.
